entries.test: Public comparisons of model capabilities, replication costs, and durable technical advantages would show whether exclusive reliance on LLMs eliminates meaningful technical barriers to competition.
entries.note: Technical moat has a plain reading as a durable technical advantage over competitors.

entries.test: Public model pricing histories and competitive analyses would show whether technically comparable offerings drive successive competitive price cuts.
entries.note: The claim asserts a causal relationship, not merely concurrent low prices.

entries.test: Benchmarks, model pricing histories, evidence of technical differentiation, and enterprise deployment surveys available at publication would test the asserted industry conditions.
entries.note: “Little permanent production use” is stronger than “not a ton of permanent inclusion in production.”
The release-year component is independently checkable. “Disappointing” supplies no shared standard, so public evidence cannot settle the whole conjunction.

entries.test: Independent evaluations of available hallucination mitigation methods across representative tasks would establish whether a reliably general solution existed at publication.
entries.note: A robust solution means reliable mitigation across uses, rather than success on one narrow benchmark.

entries.test: Financial disclosures and credible financial reporting would show whether a majority of LLM developers were operating at a loss at publication.
entries.note: “Maybe” qualifies his earlier profit prediction, not the assertion that most developers lose money.

entries.test: Public investment totals relative to US economic output and recipient companies’ spending plans would test the scale and concentration of investment in larger language models.
entries.note: The normalization drops “basically,” making the claim of a shared strategy more absolute.

entries.test: US AI funding and research allocations, alongside independent reliability evaluations at publication, would show whether LLM investment increased while alternatives remained marginal and reliability problems persisted.
entries.note: The omitted report of diminishing returns is a separate assertion.

entries.test: Public funding announcements and capital expenditure reports leading up to publication would show whether investment in the LLM/transformer approach continued to increase.
entries.note: “Every day” naturally describes continuing growth here.

entries.test: Public investment agreements, ownership disclosures, and reciprocal purchasing commitments would reveal the extent of financial interdependence and circular investment among AI companies at publication.
entries.note: “Perhaps unprecedented” hedges the historical comparison; the existence of extensive circular investment is asserted firmly.
Neither sufficient intellectual diversification nor extraordinary vulnerability has a shared test here. The causal attribution to hype does not specify a measurable outcome.
“Could well” expresses possibility. The normalization broadens the contextual target from the single LLM approach to generative AI generally.
“More likely” compares this outcome with the preceding magic scenario; “will likely” turns that relative comparison into an absolute likelihood claim.
